memory_lessons.applicability: The 2x2 mapping tests a mixed-reuse alternative to the measured four-row mapping while keeping the same CTA output footprint and thread count.
memory_lessons.claim: The four-row mapping was correct and measured 0.0147256 s; the one-row/four-column-stripe mapping was correct and measured 0.0375718 s, each with three timing samples. The baseline was correct at 0.2734839 s. These results show the mapping candidates differ in measured time, but do not establish the cause or provide register/occupancy data.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this mixed 2x2 mapping against the one-output baseline and four-row parent using the same correctness and repeated-timing protocol; collect register and occupancy diagnostics if available.

proposal.hypothesis: A 2x2 output microtile gives each thread four independent FP32 accumulators while reusing each loaded A value across two columns and each B value across two rows. Keeping a 32x32 CTA output tile and 256 threads makes this a mapping comparison with the measured four-row parent rather than a larger CTA-work comparison. The mixed mapping may reduce operand loads but its 16-column half-warp access pattern may hurt coalescing; correctness, repeated timing, and register/occupancy effects need measurement.

retained: Replace one-output-per-thread computation with a 2x2 per-thread output microtile and four independent FP32 accumulators.
Map 16x16 threads to a 32x32 output tile, reusing each loaded A value across two columns and each B value across two rows.
Guard row and column tails, use size_t element offsets, and apply alpha and beta once per valid output.
